paper_id: Steganography in animated emoji using self-reference
title: Steganography in animated emoji using self-reference
motivation: Animated emoji is widely used in OSN but lacks secure steganography; existing GIF methods are fragile against modern steganalysis.
problem_framing: How to embed secret data into animated GIF with minimal distortion by leveraging self-reference to estimate the pre-compression original image.
key_insight: If we construct a reference image close to the original image before GIF compression, we can modify pixels toward original values, reducing extra error from embedding.
method_signature: Self-reference algorithm using DnCNN to construct reference images; modify pixels based on RGB vector angles between compression and embedding distortion.
evaluation_criteria: Security evaluated by minimal total error PE using ensemble classifier with SPAM and SRMQ1 features against steganalysis.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: HILL alone is not effective for GIF due to texture simplicity, producing pepper and salt noises; method only outperforms baseline in most cases.
evidence_for_taste: obvious pepper and salt noises can be found
no obvious noises in the edge and texture areas
the data hider does not have the original content
better visual quality as well as security
thinking_moves: 把GIF压缩过程类比为添加噪声的过程,用去噪网络逆向估计原始图像
利用RGB向量的几何角度判断嵌入方向与压缩方向的相对关系,急性角被惩罚
联合帧内嵌入成本与帧间嵌入成本形成组合失真函数
借鉴通信理论中的STC框架而非单纯修改LSB
cites_own_work: Distortion function for emoji image steganography (2019)
